source.text: Περὶ δὲ τῶν παρθένων ἐπιταγὴν κυρίου οὐκ ἔχω, γνώμην δὲ δίδωμι ὡς ἠλεημένος ὑπὸ κυρίου πιστὸς εἶναι.

records.literal_gloss: Concerning now the virgins a command of [the] Lord not I have, judgment but I give as having received mercy by [the] Lord trustworthy to be.

en.L: Now concerning the virgins, I do not have a command of [the] Lord, but I give [my] judgment as one who has received mercy from [the] Lord to be trustworthy.
en.B: Now about those who have never married: I have no command from the Lord, but I give my opinion as someone the Lord in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercy has made trustworthy.
en.R: Now about people who have never married. I do not have a command from the Lord about this. But I will tell you what I think. In {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercy the Lord has made me someone you can trust.

fr.L: Or, au sujet des vierges, je n’ai pas d’ordre du Seigneur, mais je donne [mon] avis comme quelqu’un qui a reçu du Seigneur la miséricorde d’être digne de confiance.
fr.B: Au sujet de ceux qui ne se sont jamais mariés, je n’ai pas d’ordre du Seigneur, mais je donne mon avis, comme quelqu’un que le Seigneur, dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} miséricorde, a rendu digne de confiance.
fr.R: Parlons maintenant des personnes qui ne se sont jamais mariées. Je n’ai pas d’ordre du Seigneur à ce sujet. Mais je vais vous dire ce que je pense. Dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} miséricorde, le Seigneur a fait de moi quelqu’un en qui vous pouvez avoir confiance.

es.L: Ahora bien, acerca de las vírgenes, no tengo mandato del Señor, pero doy [mi] parecer como quien ha recibido misericordia del Señor para ser digno de confianza.
es.B: En cuanto a los que nunca se han casado, no tengo ningún mandato del Señor, pero doy mi opinión como alguien a quien el Señor, en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} misericordia, ha hecho digno de confianza.
es.R: Ahora hablaré de las personas que nunca se han casado. No tengo un mandato del Señor sobre esto. Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} diré lo que pienso. El Señor, en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} misericordia, ha hecho de mí alguien en quien {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} confiar.

sw.L: Basi kuhusu mabikira, sina amri ya Bwana, lakini natoa shauri [langu] kama mtu aliyehurumiwa na Bwana ili awe mwaminifu.
sw.B: Basi kuhusu wale ambao hawajawahi kufunga ndoa: sina amri kutoka kwa Bwana, lakini natoa maoni yangu kama mtu ambaye Bwana kwa huruma {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} amemfanya kuwa mwaminifu.
sw.R: Sasa kuhusu watu ambao hawajawahi kufunga ndoa. Sina amri kutoka kwa Bwana kuhusu jambo hili. Lakini nitawaambia ninavyofikiri. Kwa huruma {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} Bwana amenifanya kuwa mtu mnayeweza kumwamini.

decisions.choice: virgins: people who have never married, chiefly young women of an age to marry
alternatives: anyone who is sexually inexperienced, whatever their state
decisions.reason: παρθένος named a girl or young woman who had not yet married, and so was presumed a virgin (Matthew 1:23; Luke 1:27). The form here could be masculine or feminine, and the word can be used of men (Revelation 14:4), but in this chapter it is always a woman (7:28, 7:34, 7:36-38). Paul has already spoken to widows and the married (7:8-16); now he turns to those who have never married. In 7:36-38 the word is used of one particular young woman, and its sense there is discussed on 7:36.

decisions.choice: a command of the Lord: a saying of Jesus that settles the question
decisions.reason: In 7:10 Paul could pass on a command of the Lord about divorce (Mark 10:9-12). On the never-married he knows no such saying, so he gives his own judgment (γνώμη), as in 7:12. He does not treat it as worthless: it comes from one the Lord has made trustworthy, and in 7:40 he claims to have the Spirit of God.

decisions.choice: having received mercy to be trustworthy: the Lord's mercy has made Paul reliable
alternatives: having received mercy because he was trustworthy
decisions.reason: The perfect participle ἠλεημένος describes a mercy received in the past whose effect lasts. The infinitive "to be trustworthy" gives the result of that mercy. Paul's reliability is God's gift (1 Timothy 1:12-13), not his own claim to merit. πιστὸς here means "reliable, worthy of trust", as in 4:2.

decisions.choice: those who have never married (B); people who have never married (R)
decisions.reason: "Virgins" puts the stress on sexual experience, while Paul's question is whether such people should marry (m1). Literal keeps "virgins". "Unmarried" is kept for ἄγαμος (7:32, 7:34), which can include the widowed and divorced.

decisions.choice: my opinion (B); what I think (R)
decisions.reason: Paul sets his considered view beside a command of the Lord. "Judgment" today can sound like a verdict on someone; Literal keeps it, and 7:40 uses the same words.

decisions.choice: les vierges (L); ceux qui ne se sont jamais mariés (B); les personnes qui ne se sont jamais mariées (R); "non marié" kept for the other word (7:8, 7:32, 7:34)
decisions.reason: As in English, Balanced and Readable name a state in life rather than sexual experience (m1), and keep "not married" for the word that can include the widowed.

decisions.choice: [mon] avis (L), mon avis (B), ce que je pense (R); "mon avis" again in 7:40
decisions.reason: French "jugement" would sound like a verdict, as the English decision says of "judgment"; "avis" is the usual word for a considered view, and it is used at Literal too so that 7:40 matches.

decisions.choice: las vírgenes (L); los que nunca se han casado (B); las personas que nunca se han casado (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "vírgenes", the Greek word, through verses 25-38. The word means people who have never married, chiefly young women (m1), so Balanced and Readable say that; "solteras" would leave out the men, and "vírgenes" alone would put the weight on sexual experience rather than on marriage.

decisions.choice: parecer (L); opinión (B); lo que pienso (R)
decisions.reason: The word is Paul's considered judgment, not a command. "Parecer" says this at Literal and is used again in verse 40; "juicio" would suggest a court.

decisions.choice: mabikira (L); wale ambao hawajawahi kufunga ndoa (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mabikira" for parthenos, as Matthew 25 and Luke 1; Balanced and Readable say what the word means here, with the neutral "kufunga ndoa" since the group is not limited to women (verse 9).

decisions.choice: shauri (L); maoni (B)
decisions.reason: "Shauri" is considered advice, which is what Paul offers in place of a command; the same words return in verse 40.

source.text: νομίζω οὖν τοῦτο καλὸν ὑπάρχειν διὰ τὴν ἐνεστῶσαν ἀνάγκην, ὅτι καλὸν ἀνθρώπῳ τὸ οὕτως εἶναι.

records.literal_gloss: I think therefore this good to be because of the present necessity, that [it is] good for a man the so to be.

en.L: I think, then, that this is good because of the present distress: that [it is] good for a {{gender:person|man}} to be so.
en.B: So, because of the crisis we now face, I think this is good: it is good for a {{gender:person|man}} to stay as {{gender:they are|he is}}.
en.R: Because of the hard times we are facing now, I think it is best for you to stay as you are.

fr.L: Je pense donc que ceci est bon à cause de la détresse présente : qu’[il est] bon pour un {{gender:être humain|homme}} d’être ainsi.
fr.B: Ainsi, à cause de la crise que nous traversons, je pense que ceci est bon : il est bon pour un {{gender:être humain|homme}} de rester comme il est.
fr.R: À cause des temps difficiles que nous vivons maintenant, je pense que le mieux pour vous, c’est de rester comme vous êtes.

es.L: Pienso, pues, que esto es bueno a causa de la angustia presente: que [es] bueno para {{gender:una persona|un hombre}} estar así.
es.B: Así que, por la crisis que ahora enfrentamos, pienso que esto es bueno: es bueno que {{gender:una persona|un hombre}} se quede como está.
es.R: Por los tiempos difíciles que estamos viviendo ahora, pienso que lo mejor es que {{plural_you:se queden|os quedéis}} como {{plural_you:están|estáis}}.

sw.L: Basi nadhani hili ni jema kwa sababu ya shida iliyopo: kwamba [ni] vizuri kwa mtu kuwa hivyo.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, kwa sababu ya hali ngumu tunayokabili sasa, nadhani hili ni jema: ni vizuri mtu abaki kama alivyo.
sw.R: Kwa sababu ya nyakati ngumu tunazopitia sasa, nadhani ni bora mbaki kama mlivyo.

decisions.choice: the present distress: a time of pressure and hardship already upon the believers
alternatives: a distress that is about to come
the ordinary constraints of married life
decisions.reason: ἐνεστῶσαν is a perfect participle of a verb meaning "to stand in, to be present" (Romans 8:38; Galatians 1:4, "the present evil age"). ἀνάγκην is constraint or distress (Luke 21:23, of the hardships before the end). Paul does not say what the distress is. It may be a local hardship in Corinth, or the pressures of the last days in general; 7:29-31 links it with the shortness of the time.

decisions.choice: this is good ... that it is good: the second clause spells out what "this" is
alternatives: "because it is good", giving a reason
decisions.reason: ὅτι can mean "that" or "because". Paul starts the sentence, breaks off, and restates his point: what is good is to stay as one is. The repeated καλὸν / καλὸν shows the restart.

decisions.choice: for a person to be so: to stay in one's present state, married or unmarried
alternatives: for a man to stay unmarried
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπῳ is general: anyone. "So" points to staying as one is, the rule of 7:17-24, and 7:27 applies it both ways: the married should not seek release, and the unmarried need not seek a wife.

decisions.choice: {{gender:person|man}} (L, B); {{gender:they are|he is}} (B)
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπῳ means a human being of either sex. Readable says "you", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: the crisis we now face (B); the hard times we are facing now (R)
decisions.reason: "Distress" and "necessity" are no longer everyday words for a time of pressure. Literal keeps "present distress".

decisions.choice: {{gender:être humain|homme}} (L, B); "comme il est" without a span (B)
decisions.reason: The noun means a human being of either sex. Both French options are masculine nouns, so the pronoun after them is "il" either way and needs no span, unlike the English "they are / he is".

decisions.choice: {{gender:una persona|un hombre}}; como está, no span
decisions.reason: Spanish follows the English setting for the noun. "Está" does not show whether the person is a man or a woman, so the English second span ({{gender:they are|he is}}) has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: la angustia presente
decisions.reason: The word here means distress, a time of pressure and hardship (m1). "Necesidad" in Spanish would be heard as want or need, so Literal says "angustia".

decisions.choice: shida (L); hali ngumu (B); nyakati ngumu (R)
decisions.reason: "Dhiki" is kept for thlipsis (verse 28, as in 2 Corinthians 1), so the different Greek word here has its own Swahili word.

decisions.choice: mtu, no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: "Mtu" already means any person, man or woman.

records.literal_gloss: Have you been bound to a wife?

en.L: Have you been bound to a wife?
en.B: Are you bound to a wife?

fr.L: As-tu été lié à une femme ?

decisions.choice: bound to a wife: married
decisions.reason: δέδεσαι is the verb Paul uses of the marriage bond in 7:39 and Romans 7:2. The question is addressed to a man ("you" is singular), but the principle applies to everyone (7:28).

decisions.choice: a question that sets up a condition: "Are you married? Then ..."
alternatives: a statement: "You are bound to a wife"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates it as a question. Either way the sense is conditional: if you are married, do not seek to be free.

decisions.choice: Are you married?
alternatives: Are you bound to a wife?
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of being bound means (m1).

source.text: μὴ ζήτει λύσιν· λέλυσαι ἀπὸ γυναικός;

records.literal_gloss: Not seek release; have you been released from a wife?

en.L: Do not seek release. Have you been released from a wife?
en.B: Do not try to get free. Are you free of a wife?
en.R: Then do not try to end your marriage. Are you single?

fr.L: Ne cherche pas à être délié. As-tu été délié d’une femme ?
fr.B: Ne cherche pas à t’en libérer. Es-tu libre de toute femme ?
fr.R: Alors ne cherche pas à mettre fin à ton mariage. Es-tu célibataire ?

es.L: No busques desligarte. ¿Has quedado desligado de mujer?
es.B: No trates de liberarte. ¿Estás libre de mujer?
es.R: Entonces no intentes terminar tu matrimonio. ¿No estás casado?

sw.L: Usitafute kufunguliwa. Umefunguliwa kutoka kwa mke?
sw.B: Usijaribu kujinasua. Je, uko huru, huna mke?
sw.R: Basi usijaribu kuivunja ndoa yako. Je, huna mke?

decisions.choice: release: ending the marriage by divorce
decisions.reason: λύσιν answers "bound": the release from a marriage is divorce, which Paul has already ruled out for believers in 7:10-13.

decisions.choice: released from a wife: not married now, whether never married, widowed or divorced
decisions.reason: The perfect λέλυσαι could suggest a bond once there and now loosed. But in pairing with "bound" it most likely just means "not tied to a wife", and 7:28 speaks of the unmarried in general.

decisions.choice: try to get free; free of a wife (B); try to end your marriage; single (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the pair "get free / free" for the Greek pair "release / released". Readable says what the release is (m1) and uses an everyday word for being unmarried (m2).

decisions.choice: ligado ... desligarte ... desligado
decisions.reason: The Greek sets "bound" against "loosed", one verb family for release and having been released. Literal keeps the pair with "ligado" and "desligado", so the play on words is seen; Balanced says "unido" and "libre".

decisions.choice: Je, huna mke?
decisions.reason: "Hujaoa" would mean never married; the meaning decision includes the widowed and divorced, so Readable says "you have no wife".

en.B: Do not look for a wife.
en.R: Then do not go looking for a wife.

fr.B: Ne te mets pas en quête d’une femme.
fr.R: Alors ne pars pas à la recherche d’une femme.

es.R: Entonces no te pongas a buscar esposa.

decisions.choice: do not seek: advice, not a ban
decisions.reason: The same words as "do not seek release" make the two cases match. 7:28 shows this is counsel: marrying is not a sin.

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ γαμήσῃς, οὐχ ἥμαρτες.

records.literal_gloss: If but also you marry, not you sinned.

en.L: But if indeed you marry, you did not sin.
en.B: Yet if you do marry, you have done nothing sinful.
en.R: But if you get married, that is not a sin.

fr.L: Mais si aussi tu te maries, tu n’as pas péché.
fr.B: Pourtant, si tu te maries, tu ne commets aucun péché.
fr.R: Mais si tu te maries, ce n’est pas un péché.

es.L: Pero si también te casas, no pecaste.
es.B: Pero si te casas, no has cometido ningún pecado.
es.R: Pero si te casas, eso no es pecado.

sw.B: Hata hivyo, ukioa, hujatenda dhambi yoyote.

decisions.choice: if you marry, you have not sinned: marrying is no sin
decisions.reason: The aorist ἥμαρτες after a condition about the future looks at the act as complete: should you marry, the deed would not be a sin. Paul guards against anyone who took his advice as a rule (7:1, 7:36).

decisions.choice: you have done nothing sinful (B); that is not a sin (R)
decisions.reason: Says that the act itself is not sinful, which is the point of the aorist (m1).

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν γήμῃ ἡ παρθένος, οὐχ ἥμαρτεν.

records.literal_gloss: And if marries the virgin, not she sinned.

en.L: And if the virgin marries, she did not sin.
en.B: And if a young woman who has never married takes a husband, she has done nothing sinful.
en.R: And if a young woman who has never married gets married, that is not a sin.

fr.L: Et si la vierge se marie, elle n’a pas péché.
fr.B: Et si une jeune femme qui ne s’est jamais mariée prend un mari, elle ne commet aucun péché.
fr.R: Et si une jeune fille qui ne s’est jamais mariée se marie, ce n’est pas un péché.

es.L: Y si la virgen se casa, no pecó.
es.B: Y si una joven que nunca se ha casado toma marido, no ha cometido ningún pecado.
es.R: Y si una joven que nunca se ha casado se casa, eso no es pecado.

sw.B: Na msichana ambaye hajawahi kuolewa akiolewa, hajatenda dhambi yoyote.
sw.R: Na msichana ambaye hajawahi kuolewa akiolewa, hiyo si dhambi.

decisions.choice: the virgin: any young woman who has not yet married
decisions.reason: The article is generic: the class of such women, as in 7:25.

decisions.choice: a young woman who has never married
decisions.reason: As in 7:25 (r-en-1), the English names her state in life rather than her sexual experience.

source.text: θλῖψιν δὲ τῇ σαρκὶ ἕξουσιν οἱ τοιοῦτοι, ἐγὼ δὲ ὑμῶν φείδομαι.

records.literal_gloss: Affliction but in the flesh will have the such, I but you am sparing.

en.L: But such [people] will have affliction in the flesh, and I am sparing you.
en.B: But such people will meet hardship in this earthly life, and I am trying to spare you.
en.R: But married people will have troubles in their everyday lives, and I want to keep you from them.

fr.L: Mais de tels [gens] auront de l’affliction dans la chair, et moi, je vous épargne.
fr.B: Mais ceux-là connaîtront des difficultés dans leur vie terrestre, et je cherche à vous les épargner.
fr.R: Mais les gens mariés auront des problèmes dans leur vie de tous les jours, et je voudrais vous éviter cela.

es.L: Pero los tales tendrán aflicción en la carne, y yo {{plural_you:los|os}} estoy librando [de ella].
es.B: Pero los que se casan tendrán dificultades en esta vida terrenal, y yo quiero {{plural_you:evitárselas|evitároslas}}.
es.R: Pero los casados tendrán problemas en su vida diaria, y yo quiero {{plural_you:librarlos|libraros}} de ellos.

sw.L: Lakini watu kama hao watakuwa na dhiki katika mwili, nami ninawaepushia.
sw.B: Lakini watu kama hao watapata dhiki katika maisha haya ya duniani, nami najaribu kuwaepushia.
sw.R: Lakini watu walio katika ndoa watapata taabu katika maisha yao ya kila siku, nami nataka kuwaepusha nazo.

decisions.choice: in the flesh: in ordinary bodily, earthly life
decisions.reason: σάρξ here is not the sinful human outlook of 3:1-3 but bodily life in this world (2 Corinthians 4:11; Galatians 2:20). Those who marry will face the pressures that come with a household, all the more in "the present distress" (7:26).

decisions.choice: affliction: pressure and hardship
decisions.reason: θλῖψις is a general word for pressure and trouble. Here it is the hardship of married life in hard times, not persecution as such.

decisions.choice: I am sparing you: I want to spare you, by this advice
alternatives: I will not say more, to spare you
decisions.reason: The present φείδομαι describes what Paul is trying to do in giving this counsel.

decisions.choice: hardship in this earthly life (B); troubles in their everyday lives (R)
decisions.reason: Follows the book-wide choices for θλῖψις (affliction, hardship, trouble). "In the flesh" is said plainly (m1), since in English it suggests sinful nature.

decisions.choice: married people
decisions.reason: Readable says who "such people" are: those who marry, the subject of the two sentences before.

decisions.choice: l’affliction (L), des difficultés (B), des problèmes (R); dans la chair (L), dans leur vie terrestre (B)
decisions.reason: French follows the English steps for this word (affliction, hardship, trouble). Balanced departs from the style guide's "la chair" because here the word means ordinary bodily life (m1), and "la chair" would suggest the sinful self, as in 5:5.

decisions.choice: aflicción (L); dificultades (B); problemas (R)
decisions.reason: As the English steps from "affliction" to "hardship" and "trouble" for this word in the Corinthian letters, Literal keeps "aflicción", the word Revelation uses, and Balanced and Readable say it in plainer words.

decisions.choice: dhiki (L, B); taabu (R)
decisions.reason: The words used for thlipsis in 2 Corinthians 1; "mateso" is kept for suffering.

source.text: τοῦτο δέ φημι, ἀδελφοί, ὁ καιρὸς συνεσταλμένος ἐστίν· τὸ λοιπὸν ἵνα καὶ οἱ ἔχοντες γυναῖκας ὡς μὴ ἔχοντες ὦσιν, καὶ οἱ κλαίοντες ὡς μὴ κλαίοντες, καὶ οἱ χαίροντες ὡς μὴ χαίροντες, καὶ οἱ ἀγοράζοντες ὡς μὴ κατέχοντες, καὶ οἱ χρώμενοι τὸν κόσμον ὡς μὴ καταχρώμενοι· παράγει γὰρ τὸ σχῆμα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου.

records.literal_gloss: This now I say, brothers, the time shortened is; the remaining that both those having wives as not having be, \v 30 and those weeping as not weeping, and those rejoicing as not rejoicing, and those buying as not possessing, \v 31 and those using the world as not using fully; is passing away for the form of the world this.

en.L: But this I say, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}: the time has been shortened. From now on, [let] both those having wives be as not having, \v 30 and those weeping as not weeping, and those rejoicing as not rejoicing, and those buying as not possessing, \v 31 and those using the world as not using [it] to the full; for the form of this world is passing away.
en.B: Here is my point, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}: the time has been cut short. So from now on, married men should be as though they had no wives, \v 30 those who weep as though they did not weep, those who rejoice as though they did not rejoice, those who buy as though they kept nothing, \v 31 and those who deal with the world as though they did not use it to the full. For this world's present shape is passing away.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, this is what I mean. There is not much time left. From now on, married men should live as if they had no wives. \v 30 People who are sad should live as if they were not sad. People who are happy should live as if they were not happy. People who buy things should live as if those things were not really theirs. \v 31 People who use what this world offers should not get wrapped up in it. For this world, as it is now, is passing away.

fr.L: Mais voici ce que je dis, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} : le temps a été raccourci. Désormais, que ceux qui ont des femmes soient comme n’en ayant pas, \v 30 et ceux qui pleurent comme ne pleurant pas, et ceux qui se réjouissent comme ne se réjouissant pas, et ceux qui achètent comme ne possédant pas, \v 31 et ceux qui usent du monde comme n’en usant pas pleinement ; car la forme de ce monde passe.
fr.B: Voici où je veux en venir, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} : le temps a été abrégé. Désormais, que les hommes mariés vivent comme s’ils n’avaient pas de femme, \v 30 ceux qui pleurent comme s’ils ne pleuraient pas, ceux qui se réjouissent comme s’ils ne se réjouissaient pas, ceux qui achètent comme s’ils ne gardaient rien, \v 31 et ceux qui ont affaire au monde comme s’ils n’en profitaient pas pleinement. Car ce monde, sous sa forme actuelle, est en train de passer.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, voici ce que je veux dire. Il ne reste plus beaucoup de temps. Désormais, les hommes mariés doivent vivre comme s’ils n’avaient pas de femme. \v 30 Ceux qui sont tristes doivent vivre comme s’ils n’étaient pas tristes. Ceux qui sont heureux doivent vivre comme s’ils n’étaient pas heureux. Ceux qui achètent des choses doivent vivre comme si ces choses n’étaient pas vraiment à eux. \v 31 Ceux qui profitent de ce que le monde offre ne doivent pas s’y laisser prendre. Car ce monde, tel qu’il est maintenant, est en train de passer.

es.L: Pero esto digo, hermanos: el tiempo se ha acortado. De aquí en adelante, que también los que tienen mujer sean como si no [la] tuvieran, \v 30 y los que lloran, como si no lloraran, y los que se alegran, como si no se alegraran, y los que compran, como si no poseyeran, \v 31 y los que usan el mundo, como si no [lo] usaran a fondo; porque la forma de este mundo está pasando.
es.B: Lo que quiero decir, hermanos, es esto: el tiempo se ha acortado. Así que, de ahora en adelante, los que tienen mujer deben vivir como si no la tuvieran; \v 30 los que lloran, como si no lloraran; los que se alegran, como si no se alegraran; los que compran, como si no se quedaran con nada; \v 31 y los que tratan con el mundo, como si no lo aprovecharan del todo. Porque la forma actual de este mundo está pasando.
es.R: Hermanos, esto es lo que quiero decir: no queda mucho tiempo. De ahora en adelante, los hombres casados deben vivir como si no tuvieran esposa. \v 30 Los que están tristes deben vivir como si no estuvieran tristes. Los que están felices deben vivir como si no estuvieran felices. Los que compran cosas deben vivir como si esas cosas no fueran realmente suyas. \v 31 Los que usan lo que este mundo ofrece no deben dejarse atrapar por ello. Porque este mundo, tal como es ahora, está pasando.

sw.L: Lakini nasema hivi, ndugu: wakati umefupishwa. Tangu sasa, wale walio na wake [na] wawe kama wasio nao, \v 30 na wale wanaolia kama wasiolia, na wale wanaofurahi kama wasiofurahi, na wale wanaonunua kama wasiomiliki, \v 31 na wale wanaoutumia ulimwengu kama wasioutumia [kwa] ukamilifu; kwa maana umbo la ulimwengu huu linapita.
sw.B: Ninachomaanisha, ndugu, ni hiki: wakati umefupishwa. Kwa hiyo tangu sasa, wanaume walio na wake na wawe kama hawana wake, \v 30 wanaolia kama hawalii, wanaofurahi kama hawafurahi, wanaonunua kama hawana mali yoyote, \v 31 na wale wanaoshughulika na mambo ya ulimwengu kama hawayatumii kikamilifu. Kwa maana sura ya sasa ya ulimwengu huu inapita.
sw.R: Ndugu zangu, hiki ndicho ninachomaanisha. Hakuna muda mwingi uliobaki. Tangu sasa, wanaume walio na wake waishi kama hawana wake. \v 30 Walio na huzuni waishi kama hawana huzuni. Walio na furaha waishi kama hawana furaha. Wanaonunua vitu waishi kama vitu hivyo si mali yao kweli. \v 31 Wanaotumia mambo ya ulimwengu huu wasizame ndani yake. Kwa maana ulimwengu huu, kama ulivyo sasa, unapita.

decisions.choice: the time has been shortened: the time until the end has been drawn in, so that little remains
decisions.reason: συνεσταλμένος means drawn together or compressed. καιρός is the time God has set (Romans 13:11). Since Christ came, the present age is running out (10:11, "the ends of the ages"), and this shapes how believers hold everything in it. Paul does not name a date.

decisions.choice: from now on ... should: a call for how believers are to live
alternatives: "so that": the purpose for which God shortened the time
"the time that remains is short", joining these words to what comes before
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT places a raised dot before τὸ λοιπὸν, so these words begin the new clause. The clause with ἵνα can state God's purpose or give an instruction; either way it describes how believers are to live now.

decisions.choice: as not: living in each state without being ruled by it
alternatives: giving up marriage, grief, joy and possessions
decisions.reason: Paul does not tell husbands to leave their wives (7:10-13) or forbid weeping and rejoicing (Romans 12:15). Each "as not" means holding these things loosely, because none of them is lasting.

decisions.choice: the world: the present order of human life, with its goods, dealings and ways, which is passing
decisions.reason: κόσμος here is the world of everyday affairs that believers use and deal with: buying, owning and the like. It is not evil in itself, but it is not permanent. καταχρώμενοι means to use fully or use up; the believer uses the world without being consumed by it. σχῆμα is outward form or way of being (Philippians 2:8): the world as it now is passes away (1 John 2:17).

decisions.choice: cut short (B); there is not much time left (R)
decisions.reason: "Cut short" keeps the sense that the time has been shortened (m1); Readable says what that means for the hearers.

decisions.choice: this world's present shape (B); this world, as it is now (R)
decisions.reason: "Form" can suggest a document or a shape on paper; the point is the way the world now is (m4). Literal keeps "form".

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The address includes the whole church, women as well as men, as the book-wide choice for ἀδελφός has it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} for the readers
decisions.reason: As in English, the address includes the whole church, women as well as men.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in 1:10 and 7:24, Spanish "hermanos" already includes the sisters, so the English gender setting has no Spanish counterpart.

decisions.choice: la forma de este mundo (L); la forma actual de este mundo (B)
decisions.reason: The word is the outward shape of the present order (m4). "Forma" says that; "apariencia" could suggest that the world only seems real.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: As 1:10: "ndugu" already includes sisters.

decisions.choice: umbo (L); sura ya sasa (B)
decisions.reason: "Umbo" (form, shape) keeps the Greek picture at Literal; Balanced says "sura ya sasa" (its present appearance), as the English "present shape".

records.literal_gloss: I want but you free from care to be.

en.L: But I want you to be free from cares.
en.B: I want you to be free from cares that divide you.
en.R: I want you to be free from worry.

fr.L: Mais je veux que vous soyez sans soucis.
fr.B: Je voudrais que vous soyez libres des soucis qui vous partagent.
fr.R: Je voudrais que vous n’ayez pas d’inquiétude.

es.L: Pero quiero que {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} libres de preocupaciones.
es.B: Quiero que {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} libres de preocupaciones que {{plural_you:los|os}} dividan.

sw.L: Lakini nataka ninyi muwe bila wasiwasi.

decisions.choice: free from care: not pulled two ways by competing concerns
decisions.reason: ἀμερίμνους begins a play on the verb in the next sentences: the unmarried "care for" the things of the Lord, the married also for the things of the world. Paul does not mean that the unmarried have no concerns, but that their concern is undivided (7:33-35).

decisions.choice: free from cares that divide you
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the word "care" that the next sentences repeat, and says what kind of care is meant (m1), so that the unmarried man's "care" for the Lord does not seem to contradict this wish.

decisions.choice: sans soucis (L), libres des soucis (B); se soucier de (L), avoir souci de (B) in 7:32-34
decisions.reason: French keeps one word family for the wish and for the cares that follow, as the English keeps "care". "Avoir souci de" is not a fault, so the unmarried man's care for the Lord does not clash with Paul's wish; "s’inquiéter" would.

decisions.choice: libres de preocupaciones; se preocupa por (verses 32-34)
decisions.reason: Paul plays on one word family: free from cares, and the one who cares for the things of the Lord or of the world. Literal and Balanced keep "preocupación" and "preocuparse por" throughout so the link is heard; Readable says "piensa en" for the verb.

source.text: ὁ ἄγαμος μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κυρίου, πῶς ἀρέσῃ τῷ κυρίῳ·

records.literal_gloss: The unmarried cares for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;

en.L: The unmarried [man] cares for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord.
en.B: The unmarried man gives his care to the things of the Lord, how he may please {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: A man without a wife thinks about the things of the Lord and how to please {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Celui qui n’est pas marié se soucie des choses du Seigneur, de la façon dont il plaira au Seigneur.
fr.B: L’homme qui n’est pas marié a souci des choses du Seigneur et de la manière de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} plaire.
fr.R: Un homme qui n’a pas de femme pense aux choses du Seigneur et à la manière de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} plaire.

es.L: El no casado se preocupa por las cosas del Señor, de cómo agradará al Señor.
es.B: El hombre no casado se preocupa por las cosas del Señor, por cómo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} agradará.
es.R: Un hombre sin esposa piensa en las cosas del Señor y en cómo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} puede agradar.

sw.L: [Mwanamume] asiye na mke hujishughulisha na mambo ya Bwana, jinsi atakavyompendeza Bwana.
sw.B: Mwanamume asiye na mke huelekeza moyo wake kwa mambo ya Bwana, jinsi atakavyompendeza.
sw.R: Mwanamume asiye na mke huwaza juu ya mambo ya Bwana na jinsi ya kumpendeza.

decisions.choice: cares for the things of the Lord: gives his attention to the Lord's work and service
decisions.reason: μεριμνᾷ here is a good kind of care, as in 12:25 and Philippians 2:20. "The things of the Lord" are what concerns him: his service and his people.

decisions.choice: the unmarried man: any man without a wife
alternatives: a man who has never married
decisions.reason: ἄγαμος is broader than "virgin": in 7:8 and 7:11 it includes the widowed and the separated.

decisions.choice: gives his care to
decisions.reason: Keeps the word "care" from 7:32a and avoids "anxious", which would make his care for the Lord sound like a fault.

decisions.choice: hujishughulisha na (L); huelekeza moyo wake kwa (B); huwaza juu ya (R)
decisions.reason: The verb that was "be anxious" in verse 32a is here a good care for the Lord's work, so it is not rendered with "wasiwasi"; the same words return for the married man and woman in verses 33-34.

decisions.choice: atakavyompendeza: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Swahili marks "him" with the object prefix inside the verb, which cannot take a capital, so the English span has no counterpart.

source.text: ὁ δὲ γαμήσας μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κόσμου, πῶς ἀρέσῃ τῇ γυναικί, καὶ μεμέρισται.

records.literal_gloss: The but having married cares for the things of the world, how he may please the wife, \v 34 and he is divided.

en.L: But the [one] who married cares for the things of the world, how he may please the wife, \v 34 and he is divided.
en.B: But the married man gives his care to the things of the world, how he may please his wife, \v 34 and he is pulled two ways.
en.R: But a married man has to think about the things of this world and how to please his wife. \v 34 So he is pulled in two directions.

fr.L: Mais celui qui s’est marié se soucie des choses du monde, de la façon dont il plaira à la femme, \v 34 et il est partagé.
fr.B: Mais l’homme marié a souci des choses du monde et de la manière de plaire à sa femme, \v 34 et il est tiraillé entre les deux.
fr.R: Mais un homme marié doit penser aux choses de ce monde et à la manière de plaire à sa femme. \v 34 Alors il est tiré dans deux directions.

es.L: Pero el que se casó se preocupa por las cosas del mundo, de cómo agradará a la mujer, \v 34 y está dividido.
es.B: Pero el hombre casado se preocupa por las cosas del mundo, por cómo agradará a su mujer, \v 34 y está dividido entre las dos cosas.
es.R: Pero un hombre casado tiene que pensar en las cosas de este mundo y en cómo agradar a su esposa. \v 34 Así que se siente dividido entre dos lados.

sw.L: Lakini yeye aliyeoa hujishughulisha na mambo ya ulimwengu, jinsi atakavyompendeza mke, \v 34 naye amegawanyika.
sw.B: Lakini mwanamume aliyeoa huelekeza moyo wake kwa mambo ya ulimwengu, jinsi atakavyompendeza mkewe, \v 34 na hivyo anavutwa pande mbili.
sw.R: Lakini mwanamume aliyeoa analazimika kuwaza juu ya mambo ya ulimwengu huu na jinsi ya kumpendeza mkewe. \v 34 Kwa hiyo anavutwa pande mbili.

decisions.choice: the things of the world: the everyday affairs of this life, such as a household and its needs
decisions.reason: κόσμος here is the world of 7:31: the order of ordinary life, which is passing. Pleasing one's wife is not sin; Paul has said husband and wife owe each other care (7:3-5). The point is that a married man's attention is shared.

decisions.choice: he is divided: his attention is split between the Lord and his wife
alternatives: "the wife and the virgin are also divided (different)", joining the verb to the next words
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the sentence after μεμέρισται, so the verb completes the description of the married man. Some manuscripts join it to what follows; see the note on the next sentence.

decisions.choice: pulled two ways (B); pulled in two directions (R)
decisions.reason: "Divided" alone can suggest a split mind or a broken loyalty; the picture is of attention drawn two ways (m2).

source.text: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἡ ἄγαμος καὶ ἡ παρθένος μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κυρίου, ἵνα ᾖ ἁγία καὶ τῷ σώματι καὶ τῷ πνεύματι· ἡ δὲ γαμήσασα μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κόσμου, πῶς ἀρέσῃ τῷ ἀνδρί.

records.literal_gloss: And the woman the unmarried and the virgin cares for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in the body and in the spirit; the but having married cares for the things of the world, how she may please the husband.

en.L: And the unmarried woman and the virgin care for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in the body and in the spirit; but the [woman] who married cares for the things of the world, how she may please the husband.
en.B: And the unmarried woman, or the young woman who has never married, gives her care to the things of the Lord, so that she may be holy in body as well as in spirit. But the married woman gives her care to the things of the world, how she may please her husband.
en.R: A woman who is not married, whether she was married before or has never married, thinks about the things of the Lord. She wants to be set apart for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in body and in spirit. But a married woman has to think about the things of this world and how to please her husband.

fr.L: Et la femme non mariée et la vierge se soucient des choses du Seigneur, afin qu’elle soit sainte et de corps et d’esprit ; mais celle qui s’est mariée se soucie des choses du monde, de la façon dont elle plaira au mari.
fr.B: Et la femme qui n’est pas mariée, ou la jeune femme qui ne s’est jamais mariée, a souci des choses du Seigneur, afin d’être sainte de corps aussi bien que d’esprit. Mais la femme mariée a souci des choses du monde et de la manière de plaire à son mari.
fr.R: Une femme qui n’est pas mariée, qu’elle ait déjà été mariée ou qu’elle ne l’ait jamais été, pense aux choses du Seigneur. Elle veut être mise à part pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, dans son corps et dans son esprit. Mais une femme mariée doit penser aux choses de ce monde et à la manière de plaire à son mari.

es.L: Y la mujer no casada y la virgen se preocupan por las cosas del Señor, para ser santa tanto en el cuerpo como en el espíritu; pero la que se casó se preocupa por las cosas del mundo, de cómo agradará al marido.
es.B: Y la mujer no casada, o la joven que nunca se ha casado, se preocupa por las cosas del Señor, para ser santa tanto en el cuerpo como en el espíritu. Pero la mujer casada se preocupa por las cosas del mundo, por cómo agradará a su marido.
es.R: Una mujer que no está casada, ya sea que estuvo casada antes o que nunca se ha casado, piensa en las cosas del Señor. Quiere estar apartada para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en cuerpo y en espíritu. Pero una mujer casada tiene que pensar en las cosas de este mundo y en cómo agradar a su esposo.

sw.L: Na mwanamke asiye na mume na bikira hujishughulisha na mambo ya Bwana, ili awe mtakatifu katika mwili na katika roho; lakini yeye aliyeolewa hujishughulisha na mambo ya ulimwengu, jinsi atakavyompendeza mume.
sw.B: Na mwanamke asiye na mume, au msichana ambaye hajawahi kuolewa, huelekeza moyo wake kwa mambo ya Bwana, ili awe mtakatifu katika mwili na pia katika roho. Lakini mwanamke aliyeolewa huelekeza moyo wake kwa mambo ya ulimwengu, jinsi atakavyompendeza mumewe.
sw.R: Mwanamke ambaye hayuko katika ndoa, iwe aliwahi kuolewa au hajawahi kuolewa, huwaza juu ya mambo ya Bwana. Anataka kutengwa kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} katika mwili na katika roho. Lakini mwanamke aliyeolewa analazimika kuwaza juu ya mambo ya ulimwengu huu na jinsi ya kumpendeza mumewe.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "he is divided. And the unmarried woman and the virgin care for ..."
alternatives: "There is a difference between the wife and the virgin. The unmarried woman cares for ..."
"the unmarried woman and the unmarried virgin"
decisions.reason: The manuscripts differ here in several ways. The reading behind the King James Version joins μεμέρισται to the women ("the wife and the virgin are different") and has "the unmarried woman" begin the next clause. Other manuscripts place "unmarried" after "virgin" as well. The SBLGNT reading gives the clearest parallel to the unmarried and married man. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the unmarried woman and the virgin: a woman without a husband now (widowed or separated), and a young woman who has never married
alternatives: two names for the same woman
decisions.reason: ἄγαμος covers anyone without a spouse (7:8, 7:11), while παρθένος is the never-married woman of 7:25 and 7:28. Paul names both so that every woman without a husband is included. The singular verb treats them as one group.

decisions.choice: holy in body and spirit: wholly set apart for the Lord
decisions.reason: ἅγιος means set apart for God. "Body and spirit" means the whole person (2 Corinthians 7:1). Paul does not say married women are unholy; he has just called the believing household holy (7:14). The point is undivided devotion.

decisions.choice: whether she was married before or has never married; set apart for him
alternatives: the unmarried woman and the virgin; holy
decisions.reason: Readable says why Paul names two kinds of women (m2), and what "holy" means here (m3).

decisions.choice: roho (lowercase)
decisions.reason: The woman's own spirit, set beside her body, as 5:3; not the Holy Spirit.

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ πρὸς τὸ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν σύμφορον λέγω, οὐχ ἵνα βρόχον ὑμῖν ἐπιβάλω, ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὸ εὔσχημον καὶ εὐπάρεδρον τῷ κυρίῳ ἀπερισπάστως.

records.literal_gloss: This now for the of you yourselves benefit I say, not that a noose on you I may throw, but for the seemly and devoted to the Lord undistractedly.

en.L: Now I say this for your own benefit, not that I may throw a noose on you, but for what is seemly and devoted to the Lord without distraction.
en.B: I tell you this to help you, not to throw a noose over you. I want you to live as is fitting and to stay close beside the Lord with nothing to draw you away.
en.R: I am telling you this to help you, not to tie you down. I want you to live in a good and proper way and to give yourselves to the Lord without anything pulling you away.

fr.L: Mais je dis cela dans votre propre intérêt, non pour jeter sur vous un lacet, mais pour ce qui est convenable et attaché au Seigneur sans distraction.
fr.B: Je vous dis cela pour vous aider, non pour jeter sur vous un nœud coulant. Je veux que vous viviez comme il convient et que vous vous teniez auprès du Seigneur, sans que rien ne vous en détourne.
fr.R: Je vous dis cela pour vous aider, pas pour vous lier les mains. Je veux que vous viviez d’une manière bonne et convenable, et que vous vous donniez au Seigneur sans que rien ne vous en détourne.

es.L: Y esto digo para {{plural_you:el provecho de ustedes mismos|vuestro propio provecho}}, no para {{plural_you:echarles|echaros}} un lazo, sino para lo que es decoroso y [para] la dedicación al Señor sin distracción.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo esto para {{plural_you:ayudarlos|ayudaros}}, no para {{plural_you:echarles|echaros}} un lazo encima. Quiero que {{plural_you:vivan|viváis}} como es debido y que {{plural_you:permanezcan|permanezcáis}} junto al Señor, sin nada que {{plural_you:los|os}} distraiga.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo esto para {{plural_you:ayudarlos|ayudaros}}, no para {{plural_you:atarlos|ataros}}. Quiero que {{plural_you:vivan|viváis}} de una manera buena y correcta, y que {{plural_you:se entreguen|os entreguéis}} al Señor sin que nada {{plural_you:los|os}} aparte.

sw.L: Lakini nasema hivi kwa faida yenu wenyewe, si ili niwatupie kitanzi, bali kwa ajili ya kile kinachofaa na kujitoa kwa Bwana bila kukengeushwa.
sw.B: Nawaambia haya ili kuwasaidia, si kuwatupia kitanzi. Nataka muishi kama inavyofaa na mkae karibu na Bwana bila kitu chochote cha kuwavuta mbali.
sw.R: Nawaambia haya ili kuwasaidia, si kuwafunga. Nataka muishi kwa njia nzuri na inayofaa, na mjitoe kwa Bwana bila kitu chochote kuwavuta mbali naye.

decisions.choice: throw a noose on you: put a restraint on you, as one would catch an animal
decisions.reason: βρόχος is a noose or snare used in hunting or for restraining. Paul's advice is not meant to tie them down; marriage remains free (7:28, 7:36).

decisions.choice: what is fitting and devoted to the Lord: a life that is seemly and constantly at the Lord's service
decisions.reason: εὐσχήμων means proper or becoming. εὐπάρεδρον means sitting constantly beside someone, like an attendant waiting on a master. ἀπερισπάστως answers the "divided" man of 7:33-34: nothing drags such a person away.

decisions.choice: stay close beside the Lord with nothing to draw you away (B); give yourselves to the Lord without anything pulling you away (R)
alternatives: devotion to the Lord without distraction
decisions.reason: Keeps the picture of sitting beside the Lord (m2), and says "without distraction" in plainer words.

decisions.choice: tie you down
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday idiom with the same sense (m1).

decisions.choice: jeter sur vous un nœud coulant (B); vous lier les mains (R)
alternatives: vous passer la corde au cou
decisions.reason: The familiar French idiom "se passer la corde au cou" is a joke about getting married, which would mislead in this chapter. Balanced keeps the picture of the noose (m1); Readable uses an everyday idiom for restraint, as the English "tie you down".

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:el provecho de ustedes mismos|vuestro propio provecho}}
decisions.reason: "Su propio provecho" with ustedes could be read as someone else's benefit, so the span spells out whose it is, as the Spanish of this project does where "su" could be misread.

decisions.choice: kitanzi
decisions.reason: "Kitanzi" is a noose or snare loop, the restraint the Greek pictures; Readable says simply "kuwafunga" (tie you down).

source.text: Εἰ δέ τις ἀσχημονεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν παρθένον αὐτοῦ νομίζει ἐὰν ᾖ ὑπέρακμος, καὶ οὕτως ὀφείλει γίνεσθαι, ὃ θέλει ποιείτω· οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει· γαμείτωσαν.

records.literal_gloss: If but anyone to behave improperly toward the virgin of him thinks, if he be beyond-the-peak, and so it ought to be, what he wishes let him do; not he sins; let them marry.

en.L: But if anyone thinks he is behaving improperly toward his virgin, if he is past [the] peak, and so it ought to happen, let him do what he wishes; he does not sin; let them marry.
en.B: Now if a man thinks he is not treating the woman he is engaged to rightly, because his desire for her is strong and the marriage ought to go ahead, he may do what he wants. He commits no sin. Let the two of them marry.
en.R: Suppose a man is engaged to a young woman, and he thinks he is not being fair to her. Maybe his desire for her is too strong, and he feels they should marry. Then he should do what he wants. It is not a sin for the two of them to marry.

fr.L: Mais si quelqu’un pense se conduire de manière inconvenante envers sa vierge, si [son désir] dépasse la mesure, et qu’il doive en être ainsi, qu’il fasse ce qu’il veut ; il ne pèche pas ; qu’ils se marient.
fr.B: Si un homme pense qu’il n’agit pas correctement envers sa fiancée, parce que son désir pour elle est fort et que le mariage doit se faire, il peut faire ce qu’il veut. Il ne commet pas de péché. Qu’ils se marient tous les deux.
fr.R: Imaginons qu’un homme soit fiancé à une jeune femme, et qu’il pense ne pas être juste envers elle. Peut-être que son désir pour elle est trop fort, et qu’il pense qu’ils devraient se marier. Alors il doit faire ce qu’il veut. Ce n’est pas un péché pour eux deux de se marier.

es.L: Pero si alguno piensa que se comporta indecorosamente con su virgen, si [su deseo] está en su punto más alto, y así debe suceder, que haga lo que quiere; no peca; que se casen.
es.B: Ahora bien, si un hombre piensa que no está tratando como es debido a la mujer con la que está comprometido, porque su deseo por ella es fuerte y el matrimonio debe seguir adelante, que haga lo que quiere. No comete pecado. Que se casen los dos.
es.R: Supongamos que un hombre está comprometido con una joven y piensa que no está siendo justo con ella. Tal vez su deseo por ella es demasiado fuerte, y siente que deben casarse. Entonces que haga lo que quiere. No es pecado que los dos se casen.

sw.L: Lakini kama mtu yeyote anadhani kwamba anamtendea bikira wake isivyofaa, kama amepita kilele, na hivyo inapaswa kutokea, na afanye anachotaka; hatendi dhambi; na wafunge ndoa.
sw.B: Basi ikiwa mwanamume anadhani kwamba hamtendei ipasavyo msichana aliyemchumbia, kwa sababu tamaa yake kwake ni kubwa na ndoa inapaswa kufanyika, na afanye anavyotaka. Hatendi dhambi. Na wafunge ndoa.
sw.R: Tuseme mwanamume amemchumbia msichana, naye anaona kwamba hamtendei vyema. Huenda tamaa yake kwake ni kubwa mno, naye anaona kwamba wanapaswa kuoana. Basi afanye anavyotaka. Si dhambi kwao kuoana.

decisions.choice: his virgin: the young woman a man is engaged to marry
alternatives: his unmarried daughter, whom a father may give in marriage
a woman living with him in a marriage without sexual relations
decisions.reason: The passage can be read in two main ways. (1) A man and the woman he is engaged to: he wonders whether he is treating her rightly by holding back from marriage, and Paul says they may marry; if he is settled in mind, keeping her as she is, unmarried, is also right. (2) A father, or guardian, and his unmarried daughter: he wonders whether he is wronging her by not giving her in marriage, and Paul says he may let the couple marry. The strongest point for (2) is that γαμίζω in 7:38 elsewhere means "give in marriage" (Mark 12:25; Luke 17:27). For (1): the man's own desire and will are stressed (7:37), "his virgin" is an odd way to name a daughter, and "let them marry" most naturally means the man and the woman. A third view, that the two lived together in a celibate marriage, has little support in the text. This translation takes (1), at every level.

decisions.choice: beyond the peak: his desire is strong, at full strength or more
alternatives: she is past the usual age for marriage
decisions.reason: ὑπέρακμος means "beyond the peak". The form can refer to a man or a woman, and the subject of ᾖ is not stated. Said of the man, it means that his passion is at its height or overflowing, which fits 7:9 and the contrast in 7:37, where the man has his desire under control. Said of the woman, it means she is past the bloom of youth, which would fit the father reading.

decisions.choice: behave improperly toward her: treat her in a way that is not right or honorable
decisions.reason: ἀσχημονέω means to act in an unseemly or shameful way (13:5). It may mean keeping her waiting without marriage, or the risk of sexual sin under strong desire (7:2, 7:9). Either way, marrying ends the problem.

decisions.choice: and so it ought to be ... let them marry: if marriage is the right course, the couple should marry
decisions.reason: "So it ought to be" refers to marriage as the fitting outcome. The plural γαμείτωσαν brings in both of them: the man and the woman marry each other.

decisions.choice: the woman he is engaged to (B); a young woman he is engaged to (R)
decisions.reason: Says plainly whom "his virgin" means on the reading taken (m1). Literal keeps "his virgin", which leaves the other reading open. "Betrothed" is no longer everyday English.

decisions.choice: his desire for her is strong (B); his desire for her is too strong (R)
alternatives: if he is past the peak
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "past the peak" means on the reading taken (m2).

decisions.choice: si [son désir] dépasse la mesure (L)
alternatives: s’il a passé la fleur de l’âge
decisions.reason: French has no literal phrase for "past the peak" that leaves the sense open as the English does; a word-for-word "au-delà du sommet" means nothing. Literal follows the reading of m2 and brackets the subject it supplies; the other reading (the woman past the usual age) is in the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: sa fiancée (B); une jeune femme à qui il est fiancé (R)
decisions.reason: "Fiancée" is the everyday French word for the reading taken in m1; "promise" is old-fashioned. Literal keeps "sa vierge", which leaves the other reading open.

decisions.choice: si [su deseo] está en su punto más alto
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "if he is beyond the peak". Spanish needs a subject for the picture; Literal supplies "su deseo" in brackets, as the meaning decision reads it (m2, footnoted). "Pasado de edad" would follow the other reading, about the woman's age.

decisions.choice: su virgen (L, verses 36-38)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "his virgin" so the reader can see the word the meaning decision explains (m1); Balanced and Readable say "the woman he is engaged to".

decisions.choice: bikira wake (L); msichana aliyemchumbia (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "bikira wake" (his virgin); Balanced and Readable name the relationship the meaning decision gives, a young woman he is engaged to ("kuchumbia", to be betrothed to).

decisions.choice: kuoana
decisions.reason: "Kuoana" (marry each other) is the plain word for a couple marrying; Literal and Balanced keep "wafunge ndoa" as in verse 9.

source.text: ὃς δὲ ἕστηκεν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἑδραῖος μὴ ἔχων ἀνάγκην, ἐξουσίαν δὲ ἔχει περὶ τοῦ ἰδίου θελήματος, καὶ τοῦτο κέκρικεν ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ καρδίᾳ, τηρεῖν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ παρθένον, καλῶς ποιήσει·

records.literal_gloss: Who but stands in the heart of him firm, not having necessity, authority but has concerning the own will, and this has decided in the own heart, to keep the of himself virgin, well he will do;

en.L: But [he] who stands firm in his heart, not having necessity, but has authority over his own will, and has decided this in his own heart, to keep his own virgin, will do well.
en.B: But suppose a man stands firm in his heart. He is under no pressure, he has control over his own will, and he has decided in his own heart that the woman he is engaged to should stay as she is. He will do well.
en.R: But another man may have made up his mind firmly. He does not feel he must marry, and he is in control of what he wants. He has decided in his heart not to marry the young woman. That man will be doing what is right.

fr.L: Mais celui qui se tient ferme dans son cœur, n’ayant pas de contrainte, mais qui a autorité sur sa propre volonté, et qui a décidé cela dans son propre cœur, garder sa propre vierge, celui-là fera bien.
fr.B: Mais supposons qu’un homme se tienne ferme dans son cœur. Il n’est soumis à aucune contrainte, il est maître de sa propre volonté, et il a décidé dans son cœur que sa fiancée resterait comme elle est. Il fera bien.
fr.R: Mais un autre homme a peut-être pris fermement sa décision. Il ne sent pas qu’il doit se marier, et il est maître de ses désirs. Il a décidé dans son cœur de ne pas épouser la jeune femme. Cet homme-là agira bien.

es.L: Pero el que está firme en su corazón, no teniendo necesidad, sino que tiene autoridad sobre su propia voluntad, y ha decidido esto en su propio corazón, guardar a su propia virgen, hará bien.
es.B: Pero supongamos que un hombre se mantiene firme en su corazón. No está bajo ninguna presión, tiene dominio sobre su propia voluntad y ha decidido en su propio corazón que la mujer con la que está comprometido se quede como está. Ese hombre hará bien.
es.R: Pero otro hombre puede haber tomado una decisión firme. No siente que tenga que casarse, y es dueño de lo que quiere. Ha decidido en su corazón no casarse con la joven. Ese hombre estará haciendo lo correcto.

sw.L: Lakini yeye aliyesimama imara moyoni mwake, bila kuwa na lazima, bali ana mamlaka juu ya mapenzi yake mwenyewe, na ameamua hili moyoni mwake mwenyewe, kumtunza bikira wake, atafanya vyema.
sw.B: Lakini tuseme mwanamume amesimama imara moyoni mwake. Hana shinikizo lolote, anaweza kuyatawala mapenzi yake, na ameamua moyoni mwake kwamba msichana aliyemchumbia abaki kama alivyo. Atafanya vyema.
sw.R: Lakini mwanamume mwingine anaweza kuwa ameamua kwa uthabiti. Haoni kwamba lazima aoe, naye anaweza kutawala anachotaka. Ameamua moyoni mwake kutomwoa msichana huyo. Mwanamume huyo atakuwa anafanya lililo jema.

decisions.choice: under no necessity, with authority over his own will: not driven by desire, and free to decide
decisions.reason: ἀνάγκη is the same word as in 7:26, here an inner pressure: the strong desire of 7:36. Having ἐξουσία over his will means he is master of his desires (7:9). On the father reading, it would mean no outside pressure prevents him from deciding.

decisions.choice: to keep his virgin: to keep her as she is, that is, not to marry her
alternatives: to keep his daughter at home unmarried
decisions.reason: τηρεῖν means to keep or preserve. On the reading taken at 7:36 (m1 there), the man chooses not to marry. On the father reading, he keeps his daughter unmarried.

decisions.choice: that the woman he is engaged to should stay as she is
alternatives: to keep her as his betrothed
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the reading taken at 7:36 and says what keeping her means without going beyond the Greek. Readable says it plainly: "not to marry the young woman".

decisions.choice: He does not feel he must marry
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pressure is (m1).

decisions.choice: mamlaka juu ya mapenzi yake (L); kuyatawala mapenzi yake (B); kutawala anachotaka (R)
decisions.reason: "Mapenzi" here is his will, not romantic love; Readable avoids the ambiguity with "anachotaka" (what he wants).

source.text: ὥστε καὶ ὁ γαμίζων τὴν παρθένον ἑαυτοῦ καλῶς ποιεῖ, καὶ ὁ μὴ γαμίζων κρεῖσσον ποιήσει.

records.literal_gloss: So that both the marrying the virgin of himself well does, and the not marrying better will do.

en.L: So then, both the [one] marrying his own virgin does well, and the [one] not marrying will do better.
en.B: So the man who marries the woman he is engaged to does well, and the man who does not marry her will do better.
en.R: So a man who marries the young woman he is engaged to is doing a good thing. And a man who does not marry will be doing something even better.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, celui qui épouse sa propre vierge fait bien, et celui qui ne [l’]épouse pas fera mieux.
fr.B: Ainsi, l’homme qui épouse sa fiancée fait bien, et celui qui ne l’épouse pas fera mieux.
fr.R: Donc un homme qui épouse la jeune femme à qui il est fiancé fait une bonne chose. Et un homme qui ne se marie pas fera quelque chose d’encore mieux.

es.L: De modo que el que se casa con su propia virgen hace bien, y el que no se casa hará mejor.
es.B: Así que el hombre que se casa con la mujer con la que está comprometido hace bien, y el que no se casa con ella hará mejor.
es.R: Así que un hombre que se casa con la joven con la que está comprometido hace algo bueno. Y un hombre que no se casa hará algo todavía mejor.

sw.L: Hivyo basi, yeye anayemwoa bikira wake anafanya vyema, na yeye asiyemwoa atafanya vyema zaidi.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo mwanamume anayemwoa msichana aliyemchumbia anafanya vyema, na yule asiyemwoa atafanya vyema zaidi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo mwanamume anayemwoa msichana aliyemchumbia anafanya jambo jema. Na mwanamume asiyeoa atakuwa anafanya jambo bora zaidi.

decisions.choice: marrying: taking her as his wife
alternatives: giving her in marriage, as a father gives his daughter
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in the New Testament γαμίζω means "give in marriage" (Mark 12:25; Luke 17:27), and that is the main support for the father reading of 7:36-38. On the reading taken at 7:36 (m1 there), Paul uses it here for the man who marries. The choice follows that decision.

decisions.choice: well ... better: both choices are good; not marrying is better in view of the present time
decisions.reason: Paul has given his reasons in 7:26-35: the present distress, the shortness of the time and undivided devotion to the Lord. He has also said marriage is no sin (7:28, 7:36) and that each person has his own gift (7:7).

source.text: Γυνὴ δέδεται ἐφ’ ὅσον χρόνον ζῇ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς· ἐὰν δὲ κοιμηθῇ ὁ ἀνήρ, ἐλευθέρα ἐστὶν ᾧ θέλει γαμηθῆναι, μόνον ἐν κυρίῳ·

records.literal_gloss: A wife is bound for as much time as lives the husband of her; if but falls asleep the husband, free she is to whom she wishes to be married, only in [the] Lord;

en.L: A wife is bound for as long a time as her husband lives; but if the husband falls asleep, she is free to be married to whom she wishes, only in [the] Lord.
en.B: A wife remains bound for as long as her husband is living. Should her husband die, she is free to marry whomever she wants, though only a man who belongs to the Lord.
en.R: A wife is joined to her husband for as long as he is alive. But if he dies, she may marry anyone she wants, as long as he is a follower of the Lord.

fr.L: Une femme est liée aussi longtemps que vit son mari ; mais si le mari s’endort, elle est libre de se marier à qui elle veut, seulement dans le Seigneur.
fr.B: Une femme reste liée tant que son mari est en vie. Si son mari meurt, elle est libre d’épouser qui elle veut, mais seulement un homme qui appartient au Seigneur.
fr.R: Une femme est unie à son mari aussi longtemps qu’il est vivant. Mais s’il meurt, elle peut épouser l’homme qu’elle veut, pourvu que ce soit quelqu’un qui suit le Seigneur.

es.L: [La] mujer está ligada todo el tiempo que vive su marido; pero si el marido se duerme, es libre para casarse con quien quiera, solo en [el] Señor.
es.B: La mujer está ligada a su marido mientras él vive. Si su marido muere, queda libre para casarse con quien quiera, pero solo con un hombre que pertenezca al Señor.
es.R: Una esposa está unida a su esposo mientras él esté vivo. Pero si él muere, ella puede casarse con quien quiera, siempre que él también pertenezca al Señor.

sw.L: Mke amefungwa kwa muda wote ambao mume wake yu hai; lakini mume akilala, yuko huru kuolewa na yeyote amtakaye, ila tu katika Bwana.
sw.B: Mke anabaki amefungwa kwa muda wote mumewe akiwa hai. Mumewe akifariki, yuko huru kuolewa na yeyote amtakaye, ila awe mtu aliye wa Bwana tu.
sw.R: Mke ameunganishwa na mumewe muda wote mumewe akiwa hai. Lakini mumewe akifa, anaweza kuolewa na mtu yeyote anayemtaka, ilimradi mtu huyo ni mfuasi wa Bwana.

decisions.choice: falls asleep: dies
decisions.reason: κοιμάομαι is a common way of speaking of the death of believers (11:30; 15:6, 15:18; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-15).

decisions.choice: only in the Lord: she must marry a fellow believer
alternatives: she must marry in a Christian way, whoever the husband is
decisions.reason: "In the Lord" describes one who belongs to Christ (Romans 16:8-13). The limit most naturally applies to the man she marries. Paul allowed believers already married to unbelievers to stay married (7:12-14); this is about entering a new marriage (2 Corinthians 6:14).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "a wife is bound"
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts add "by law", probably from Romans 7:2. The sense is not changed. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: dies
decisions.reason: The idiom (m1) is said plainly; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: only a man who belongs to the Lord (B); as long as he is a follower of the Lord (R)
decisions.reason: Says what "in the Lord" means here (m2).

decisions.choice: s’endort (L); meurt (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the idiom for death, which French readers know from church use; Balanced and Readable say it plainly (m1).

decisions.choice: se duerme (L); muere (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of falling asleep for dying (m1), which Spanish readers know from the Bible; Balanced and Readable say "muere", as the English does.

decisions.choice: akilala
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of falling asleep, which Swahili Christian speech also uses for dying; Balanced "akifariki" and Readable "akifa" say it plainly, as the English.

source.text: μακαριωτέρα δέ ἐστιν ἐὰν οὕτως μείνῃ, κατὰ τὴν ἐμὴν γνώμην, δοκῶ δὲ κἀγὼ πνεῦμα θεοῦ ἔχειν.

records.literal_gloss: More blessed but she is if so she remains, according to the my judgment; I think but I also [the] Spirit of God to have.

en.L: But she is more blessed if she remains so, according to my judgment; and I think that I also have [the] Spirit of God.
en.B: Even so, in my opinion she is more blessed if she remains a widow. And I believe that I too have the Spirit of God.
en.R: But I think she will be better off if she does not marry again. And I believe God's Spirit is guiding me too.

fr.L: Mais elle est plus heureuse si elle demeure ainsi, selon mon avis ; et je pense que moi aussi, j’ai l’Esprit de Dieu.
fr.B: Malgré tout, à mon avis, elle est plus heureuse si elle reste veuve. Et je crois que moi aussi, j’ai l’Esprit de Dieu.
fr.R: Mais je pense qu’elle sera plus heureuse si elle ne se remarie pas. Et je crois que l’Esprit de Dieu me guide, moi aussi.

es.L: Pero más dichosa es si permanece así, según mi parecer; y pienso que también yo tengo [el] Espíritu de Dios.
es.B: Aun así, en mi opinión será más dichosa si sigue viuda. Y creo que también yo tengo el Espíritu de Dios.
es.R: Pero yo pienso que estará mejor si no se vuelve a casar. Y creo que el Espíritu de Dios también me guía a mí.

sw.L: Lakini ana heri zaidi akibaki hivyo, kwa kadiri ya shauri langu; nami nadhani kwamba mimi pia nina Roho wa Mungu.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, kwa maoni yangu, ana heri zaidi akibaki mjane. Nami naamini kwamba mimi pia nina Roho wa Mungu.
sw.R: Lakini nadhani atakuwa na maisha bora zaidi asipoolewa tena. Nami naamini kwamba Roho wa Mungu ananiongoza pia.

decisions.choice: more blessed: better off, in the fuller sense of a life given to the Lord without distraction
decisions.reason: μακάριος is the word of the Beatitudes (Matthew 5:3-11). Paul's reasons for preferring that she stay unmarried are those of 7:26-35, not merely her contentment.

decisions.choice: I think that I too have the Spirit of God: a modest but firm claim to the Spirit's guidance
alternatives: real uncertainty about whether he has the Spirit
decisions.reason: δοκῶ is restrained, perhaps with irony, and κἀγὼ ("I too") suggests that some in Corinth claimed the Spirit for their own views (14:37). Paul's opinion is not a command of the Lord (7:25), but it is given by one led by God's Spirit (2:12-16).

decisions.choice: if she remains a widow (B); if she does not marry again (R)
decisions.reason: Says what "so" refers to: the widow of 7:39 staying unmarried.

decisions.choice: God's Spirit is guiding me too
alternatives: I too have the Spirit of God
decisions.reason: Readable says what having the Spirit means for Paul's advice (m2).

decisions.choice: plus heureuse (every level)
decisions.reason: "Heureux" is the usual French for this word, as in the Beatitudes; "bienheureux" now sounds like church language. It keeps the fuller sense of m1 better than "mieux lotie".

decisions.choice: más dichosa
decisions.reason: "Dichoso" is the Spanish word this project uses for blessed; here it means better off in a life given to the Lord (m1), which "más feliz" would narrow to a feeling.

decisions.choice: ana heri zaidi
decisions.reason: "Heri" is the settled word for makarios (blessed, well off), as in the Beatitudes; Readable says "maisha bora zaidi" (better off), as the English Readable.
